##### SUMMARY
<!--- Explain the problem briefly below -->
The `ini` lookup plugin still uses the archaic, problematic "string-passing" argument method, not the newer standard mentioned [here](https://github.com/ansible/proposals/issues/15#issuecomment-367022542).

The most recent work (that I can find) that changes argument handling is #16477, which simply implements a hack to work around spaces in arguments.

review_comments: should this still check if `params[x]` is truthy for inclusion?
not sure we want to add truthiness to this as 'false' positives are possible.

The comment is right, but there's a little change in behavior where something like
```
- debug: msg="{{ lookup('ini', 'file=users.ini', 'user', section='integration') }}"
```
```
# users.ini
[integration]
user=test
```
'works' and also returns the value of 'user' with a comma.
```
ok: [localhost] => {
    "msg": ",test"
}
```

@bcoca the order matters too, did you copy/paste? It may not matter anyway, I just made a contrived example to depict the change and I stopped looking before determining if there was a more reasonable way someone might stumble upon it or rely on it.
yes, for the 2nd one
Shouldn't this only be called if the set_options in line 145 was never called? Otherwise strings behind a dictionary entry would overwrite the options provided in the dictionary.
yes ... i made comments to that effect, but this is only way i saw of keeping backwards compat
Can this happen at all, since you added `type: list`?
not for the config route, but yes for the 'inline dict' .. again keeping backwards compatibility here.
But the inline dict route now also uses the config manager.
sorry, inline string, not dict .. this lookup allowed for many bad ways of specifying params

Hmm, I still don't see where that should happen :) Right now, `_split_on` is only called on the results of `self.get_option('files')` and `self.get_option('paths')`, so only for data that went through ConfigManager.

they can still be inline strings at that point, since it was allowed before, it is only way to continue to allow for that

files and path CAN be a list or can be char separated string, in the case of paths 2 chars, in files 3 (but , is taken care of automatically by type: list, so just need the other 2)

```- hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
  - name: test legacy formats
    set_fact: hatethisformat={{item}}
    vars:
      params:
        files: not/a/file.yaml;hosts
        paths: not/a/path:/etc
    loop: "{{ q('first_found', params) }}"```
Wow, that's not just copy'n'paste error prone, but also pretty inefficient. Thanks for replacing that :)
not fully replaced, keeping backwards compat, but now we can move away from it.
If it's getting deprecated for 2.18 and the idea is to have a long transition period for users, should we display the deprecation warning for 2.12/2.13?
no, for now I want to go over all examples and convert first, then maybe enable in next version

Since this function is no longer used, and is private, why not simply make its `version` argument mandatory instead of having more code that runs when `constants` is importet? (Or remove this completely, though it might be useful again in the future.)

it is used (at least in this file) and .. sadly as much as we flag them private .. many still ref them, so i prefer backwards compat and eventually deprecate this deprecate function when we don't use it anymore

Didn't see a comment about this, but something like this would now work
```
files:
  - not/a/file.yaml;also/not.yml
  - nope.yml;hosts
paths: /etc
```
... need to deprecate the 'custom separators' as soon as i can ...
